title: Quebec, from the opposite shore of the St. Lawrence
artist: William Henry Bartlett (drawn c. 1838), steel engraving published by George Virtue
what_it_shows: Quebec and the Citadel seen from the Lévis shore, square-riggers in the river, a habitant cart and cattle in the foreground.
how_close: The exact spot: the Pointe-Lévy shore, drawn a year or three before the Lamberts left Lauzon in 1841.
source_note: N. P. Willis, Canadian Scenery Illustrated, vol. 1 (London: George Virtue, 1842), University of Toronto Fisher Library scan, JP2 leaf 105.
rights: Public domain (published 1840-42; Bartlett d. 1854). Internet Archive scan, no restrictions.
credit_line: W. H. Bartlett, "Quebec, from the opposite shore of the St. Lawrence," in N. P. Willis, Canadian Scenery Illustrated, vol. 1 (London: George Virtue, 1842). Internet Archive / University of Toronto Fisher Library.
fit: Bartlett drew Pointe-Lévy c.1838, published 1840-42: place exact, era exact for the 1841 departure. OK.

title: The Three Rivers (River St. Lawrence)
artist: William Henry Bartlett, steel engraving by R. Wallis
what_it_shows: Travellers crowding into boats at Trois-Rivières, with a steamboat under smoke and sailing craft on the St. Lawrence.
how_close: Same river, same decade: the Quebec-Montreal steamer run the family took first, drawn c. 1838-40.
source_note: Canadian Scenery Illustrated, vol. 1, JP2 leaf 304.
rights: Public domain (published 1840-42). Internet Archive scan, no restrictions.
credit_line: W. H. Bartlett, "The Three Rivers," in N. P. Willis, Canadian Scenery Illustrated, vol. 1 (London: George Virtue, 1842). Internet Archive / University of Toronto Fisher Library.
fit: Trois-Rivières c.1838-40 on the route the family took: place on route, era exact. OK.

title: Long Sault Rapid, on the St. Lawrence
artist: William Henry Bartlett, steel engraving
what_it_shows: The Long Sault rapids above Cornwall, figures on the rocky shore.
how_close: The exact rapids the 1841 guides say the stage went around ('stage past the Long Sault'), drawn c. 1838-40.
source_note: Canadian Scenery Illustrated, vol. 1, JP2 leaf 99. Alternate for beat 2 alongside 'lawrence'.
rights: Public domain (published 1840-42). Internet Archive scan, no restrictions.
credit_line: W. H. Bartlett, "Long Sault Rapid, on the St. Lawrence," in N. P. Willis, Canadian Scenery Illustrated, vol. 1 (London: George Virtue, 1842). Internet Archive / University of Toronto Fisher Library.
fit: Long Sault c.1838-40: place on route, era exact. OK.

title: City of Detroit, Michigan, Taken from the Canada Shore near the Ferry
artist: William James Bennett after Frederick K. Grain, hand-coloured aquatint
what_it_shows: Side-wheel lake steamers, schooners and the Detroit waterfront from the Canadian bank.
how_close: Detroit was the first big call on the Buffalo-Chicago run; four years before the Lamberts' passage, and these are the boats of that line.
source_note: National Gallery of Art, Washington, acc. 1985.64.124; file via Wikimedia Commons (NGA open-access donation).
rights: CC0 / public domain (NGA Open Access).
credit_line: William James Bennett after Frederick K. Grain, "City of Detroit, Michigan, Taken from the Canada Shore near the Ferry," 1837. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Open Access.
fit: Detroit 1837, four years early, one port of call on the Buffalo-Chicago run: era close, place on route. OK.

title: Alton, Illinois
artist: Henry Lewis, tinted lithograph (Arnz & Co., Düsseldorf) from his 1846-48 sketches
what_it_shows: A steamboat at the Alton landing below the town's churches and warehouses.
how_close: Alton is where Davison's 1840 guide lands the Illinois River boats before the last 21 miles to St. Louis; sketched seven years after the Lamberts passed. No period image of the Chicago-Peru stage was found.
source_note: Das illustrirte Mississippithal, Missouri Historical Society N45831, via DPLA / Wikimedia Commons.
rights: No Known Copyright (Missouri Historical Society, rightsstatements.org NKC); work published 1854-57, public domain.
credit_line: Henry Lewis, "Alton, Illinois," from Das illustrirte Mississippithal (Düsseldorf, 1854-57). Missouri Historical Society.
fit: Alton, sketched 1848 and published 1854-57: 7-16 years late, and Alton is the Illinois River's mouth, not the Chicago-Peru stage or Peru itself. FLAG (place partial). No replacement found.

title: Southeast View of St. Louis from the Illinois Shore, with the steamer St. Louis
artist: John Caspar Wild, lithograph (photograph of the coloured print)
what_it_shows: The St. Louis levee and skyline across the Mississippi, the side-wheeler St. Louis in the foreground.
how_close: The same waterfront, drawn the year before the Lamberts wintered there (1841-42).
source_note: Missouri Historical Society P0052-00047, via DPLA / Wikimedia Commons.
rights: No Copyright - United States (Missouri Historical Society, rightsstatements.org NoC-US); published 1840.
credit_line: J. C. Wild, "Southeast View of St. Louis from the Illinois Shore," 1840. Missouri Historical Society.
fit: St. Louis waterfront 1840, the year before their 1841-42 winter: place exact, era exact. OK.

title: Fort Snelling
artist: Henry Lewis, tinted lithograph from his 1848 sketch
what_it_shows: The fort on its bluff above the meeting of the Mississippi and Minnesota rivers, a Dakota lodge in the foreground.
how_close: The landing under this fort is where the 1842 boat trip ended; sketched six years later, before anything much had changed.
source_note: Das illustrirte Mississippithal, Missouri Historical Society N45834, via DPLA / Wikimedia Commons.
rights: No Known Copyright (Missouri Historical Society); published 1854-57, public domain.
credit_line: Henry Lewis, "Fort Snelling," from Das illustrirte Mississippithal (Düsseldorf, 1854-57). Missouri Historical Society.
fit: Fort Snelling sketched 1848, published 1854-57: place exact, 6 years after 1842 by the sketch date, 12-15 by publication. OK (borderline on publication date).

title: Fort Garry and St. Boniface (Red River Settlement)
artist: Paul Kane, oil on canvas from his June 1846 sketches
what_it_shows: The Red River at the Forks: Fort Garry's walls, St. Boniface's twin-towered cathedral across the water, a settler's fence and cart in front.
how_close: St. Boniface as it looked in June 1846, a year after the Lamberts left Bishop Provencher's parish. Only a 1200 px copy was available; not enlarged.
source_note: National Gallery of Canada; file via Wikimedia Commons.
rights: Public domain (Kane d. 1871; PD-Art).
credit_line: Paul Kane, "Fort Garry and St. Boniface," c. 1851-56. National Gallery of Canada.
fit: Fort Garry and St. Boniface sketched 1846, painted 1851-56: place exact, a year after they left. OK.

title: Camping on the Prairie
artist: Paul Kane, oil on paper
what_it_shows: A tent, a saddle horse and a Red River cart at a camp on the open prairie near Fort Garry.
how_close: A cart camp on the Red River prairie in June 1846, one year after the Lamberts' brigade went south; Kane's own camp on the way to the buffalo hunt.
source_note: Stark Museum of Art, Orange, Texas. File via Wikimedia Commons, scanned from Eaton & Urbanek, Paul Kane's Great Nor-West (UBC Press, 1995).
rights: Public domain (Kane d. 1871; PD-Art). Stark Museum page could not be reached to confirm its own image terms; the Commons scan is from a book, not the museum.
credit_line: Paul Kane, "Camping on the Prairie," 1846. Stark Museum of Art, Orange, Texas.
fit: Kane's Red River prairie camp, 1846: one year after, same country. OK.

title: Red River Ox Carts on Main Street in St. Anthony
artist: Unknown photographer (photograph of the original daguerreotype)
what_it_shows: A train of Red River carts and oxen on the plank road at St. Anthony Falls, the first suspension bridge in the distance.
how_close: The last miles of the Woods Trail, which came down the east bank to St. Anthony Falls and St. Paul; a decade after 1845, the same carts and the same road.
source_note: Hennepin County Library, Edward A. Bromley Photographs, EB1319 / BR0134; via DPLA / Wikimedia Commons.
rights: No Copyright - United States (Hennepin County Library, rightsstatements.org NoC-US). Attribution requested: "Hennepin County Library."
credit_line: "Red River Ox Carts on Main Street in St. Anthony," 1850s. Hennepin County Library, Edward A. Bromley Collection.
fit: Red River carts in St. Anthony, 1850s: same trail, about a decade later, at its end (St. Anthony), not along the Woods Trail. OK, minor place caveat.

title: St. Paul's im Menesotah Territorium (St. Paul in 1848)
artist: Henry Lewis, tinted lithograph from his 1848 sketch
what_it_shows: The handful of buildings and the chapel on the St. Paul bluff above the Mississippi, a Dakota woman seated under the trees.
how_close: St. Paul three years after the Lamberts settled on Lake Gervais seven miles north; the nearest town to Little Canada, as they knew it.
source_note: Das illustrirte Mississippithal (Düsseldorf, 1857), University of Illinois copy; plate image via Internet Archive Book Images (Flickr 14774610794) / Wikimedia Commons.
rights: Public domain (published 1854-57). Internet Archive Book Images, no known copyright restrictions.
credit_line: Henry Lewis, "St. Paul's im Menesotah Territorium," from Das illustrirte Mississippithal (Düsseldorf, 1854-57). Internet Archive.
fit: St. Paul sketched 1848, published 1854-57: three years after they settled, place exact. OK.

title: Church at Point Levi
artist: William Henry Bartlett, steel engraving
what_it_shows: The parish church of Saint-Joseph-de-la-Pointe-Lévy above the St. Lawrence, Quebec's cliffs beyond, two figures on the bank.
how_close: The Lamberts' own parish church, drawn about 1840, the year before they left.
caption: The church at Pointe-Lévy, the Lambert parish, drawn by Bartlett about 1840, the year before the family left.
source_note: Canadian Scenery Illustrated, vol. 2 (London: George Virtue, 1842), University of Toronto Fisher Library scan, JP2 leaf 79.
rights: Public domain (published 1840-42). Internet Archive scan, no restrictions.
credit_line: W. H. Bartlett, "Church at Point Levi," in N. P. Willis, Canadian Scenery Illustrated, vol. 2 (London: George Virtue, 1842). Internet Archive / University of Toronto Fisher Library.
fit: Point Levi church c.1840: their parish church, place and era exact. OK.

title: Québec vu de la Pointe de Lévy (Quebec seen from Pointe-Lévy)
artist: Cornelius Krieghoff, oil on canvas
what_it_shows: The Lévis heights with habitant figures looking across the St. Lawrence to Quebec.
how_close: The Lamberts' shore, two decades after they left; the fields and the view had not changed much. Source copy 1070 px, enlarged 1.3x.
caption: Habitants on the Lévis shore looking across to Quebec, painted by Krieghoff in 1863, the Lamberts' own shore a generation on.
source_note: Montreal Museum of Fine Arts, acc. 1954.1103, Mary Fry Dawson Bequest.
rights: Public domain (Krieghoff d. 1872; PD-Art).
credit_line: Cornelius Krieghoff, "Québec vu de la Pointe de Lévy," 1863. Montreal Museum of Fine Arts, Mary Fry Dawson Bequest.
fit: Krieghoff 1863, Quebec from Pointe-Lévy: place exact, 22 years after 1841 (fine for the 1820-41 life set's later end, 22-43 years off its start). Borderline; FLAG lightly. The 1840s Bartlett "Quebec from the opposite shore" (already the levis beat) is the in-period equivalent.

title: Settler's Log House
artist: Cornelius Krieghoff, oil on canvas
what_it_shows: A habitant family's log house in the snow near Quebec, with a sleigh, children and dogs in the yard.
how_close: A French-Canadian farm household near Quebec, painted fifteen years after the Lamberts left; the kind of house, not their house.
caption: A habitant log house near Quebec in winter, painted by Krieghoff in 1856; a household like the one the Lamberts left in 1841.
source_note: Art Gallery of Ontario, purchased with funds from the Reuben Wells Leonard Estate, 1937; image from Google Art Project.
rights: Public domain (Krieghoff d. 1872; PD-Art).
credit_line: Cornelius Krieghoff, "Settler's Log House," 1856. Art Gallery of Ontario, via Google Art Project.
fit: Krieghoff 1856 settler's log house near Quebec: 15-36 years after the c.1820-41 span, generic habitant household, not Lauzon. FLAG (generic place). No replacement found.

title: Winter Landscape, Laval
artist: Cornelius Krieghoff, oil on canvas
what_it_shows: A frozen river road below the Laurentians, habitants with sleighs and a farmhouse at the left.
how_close: Winter travel and farm life in the Quebec countryside, two decades on; same way of life, not the same parish.
caption: A habitant farm and sleigh road in the Quebec winter, Krieghoff 1862; the life the Lamberts grew up in.
source_note: National Gallery of Canada, acc. 5886; file via Wikimedia Commons.
rights: Public domain (Krieghoff d. 1872; PD-Art).
credit_line: Cornelius Krieghoff, "Winter Landscape, Laval," 1862. National Gallery of Canada.
fit: Krieghoff 1862 winter at Laval: 21-42 years after the span, and Laval is near Montreal, not the Quebec/Lauzon shore. FLAG (wrong place; era more than 20 years off). No replacement found.

title: A Dog Cariole, only used in winter by Canadian Indians
artist: Peter Rindisbacher, watercolour and ink
what_it_shows: A dog team hauling a cariole across the snow at the Red River Settlement, a driver on snowshoes ahead.
how_close: Red River winter travel drawn at the settlement itself, seventeen years before the Lamberts arrived.
caption: Winter travel at the Red River Settlement, drawn there by Rindisbacher in 1825, a generation before the Lamberts' St. Boniface years.
source_note: Art Gallery of Ontario; file via Wikimedia Commons.
rights: Public domain (Rindisbacher d. 1834; PD-Canada, PD-US).
credit_line: Peter Rindisbacher, "A Dog Cariole only used in winter by Canadian Indians," 1825. Art Gallery of Ontario.
fit: Rindisbacher 1825 at Red River: place exact, 17 years before the 1842-45 St. Boniface years. OK (inside ~30 years).

title: Half-Breeds Running Buffalo (the Métis buffalo hunt)
artist: Paul Kane, oil on canvas from his June 1846 sketches
what_it_shows: Métis hunters from Red River running buffalo on the plains south of the settlement; the fallen rider is Kane himself.
how_close: The summer hunt out of Red River and Pembina in June 1846, the year after the Lamberts left; the Ducharmes' Métis world.
caption: The Métis summer buffalo hunt out of Red River, June 1846, painted by Kane, who rode with it a year after the Lamberts went south.
source_note: Royal Ontario Museum, Toronto.
rights: Public domain (Kane d. 1871; PD-Art).
credit_line: Paul Kane, "Half-Breeds Running Buffalo," 1846. Royal Ontario Museum.
fit: Kane's Métis buffalo hunt, sketched 1846: place exact (Red River/Pembina), one year after. OK.

title: Indian Sugar Camp
artist: Seth Eastman (drawn at Fort Snelling, 1840s), engraved by John C. McRae
what_it_shows: Dakota women boiling maple sap in a sugar bush, bark lodges and kettles among the trees.
how_close: Dakota spring life in the Fort Snelling country while the Lamberts were settling; the neighbours of the first Little Canada farms.
caption: Dakota maple sugaring near Fort Snelling, drawn by Seth Eastman in the 1840s; the spring work of the Lamberts' nearest neighbours.
source_note: Library of Congress Prints & Photographs, cph.3c15628; file via Wikimedia Commons.
rights: Public domain (published 1853). Library of Congress: no known restrictions on publication.
credit_line: Seth Eastman, "Indian Sugar Camp," engraved by John C. McRae, 1853. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division.
fit: Eastman, Dakota sugar camp, drawn 1841-48, published 1853: Fort Snelling country, era exact for 1845-75 Little Canada. OK; it shows Dakota life, not the French-Canadian settlement.

title: City of St. Paul, Capital of Minesota [sic]
artist: Max Strobel (del.), James Fuller Queen (lithographer), P. S. Duval & Co., Philadelphia
what_it_shows: St. Paul on its bluffs from across the Mississippi, a steamboat at the landing, the town eight years after the Lamberts came.
how_close: The market town seven miles south of Lake Gervais, as it stood in 1853.
caption: St. Paul in 1853, eight years after the Lamberts took up section 8 on Lake Gervais, seven miles north.
source_note: Library of Congress Prints & Photographs, pga.07963; file via Wikimedia Commons.
rights: Public domain (published 1853). Library of Congress: no known restrictions on publication.
credit_line: Strobel / J. Queen, "City of St. Paul, Capital of Minesota," P. S. Duval & Co., 1853. Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division.
fit: St. Paul 1853: town seven miles off, era inside 1845-75. OK.

title: The Chapel of St. Paul (Father Galtier's log chapel of 1841)
artist: Unknown photographer
what_it_shows: The squared-log chapel Lucien Galtier built in 1841, with a drugstore sign beside it; the building that named the town.
how_close: The French-Canadian parish church of the Lamberts' first years in Minnesota, photographed about a decade after it was built (it was taken down in 1856). Source copy 800 px, enlarged 1.5x.
caption: Father Galtier's 1841 log chapel of St. Paul, photographed about 1851; the church that served the French-Canadian settlers before Little Canada had its own.
source_note: Commons copy credits cathedralheritagefoundation.org; the holding archive is not named there (most likely Minnesota Historical Society). Worth replacing with an MNHS scan if one can be downloaded.
rights: Public domain in the US (photograph published before 1930; Commons PD-US-expired). Holder not confirmed.
credit_line: "Chapel of St. Paul," photograph, c. 1851. Via Cathedral Heritage Foundation / Wikimedia Commons.
fit: Galtier's 1841 chapel photographed c.1851-55: their first parish, era inside. OK; photographer and holder unconfirmed (rights note already says so).

title: Boulongne
artist: Christophe Tassin (etching, Les plans et profils des principales villes de France)
what_it_shows: Boulogne from the landward hills: the walled upper town with its cathedral and belfry, the lower town by the harbour, the Roman lighthouse (Tour d'Odre) on the cliff, ships in the Channel and the English coast on the horizon.
how_close: Boulogne itself, engraved when Eustache was about 17.
source_note: Commons file from the Bibliothèque municipale de Reims (P 2781), uploaded by G. Garitan; 2981x2074.
rights: Public domain: Commons page carries {{PD-old}}, LicenseShortName "Public domain"; Tassin d. 1660.
credit_line: Christophe Tassin, "Boulongne," Les plans et profils des principales villes et lieux considérables de France (Paris, 1634). Bibliothèque municipale de Reims, via Wikimedia Commons.
fit: Boulogne 1634, about ten years before he left: place exact, era exact.

title: Navis Mercatoria Hollandica, vulgo Vliet (Dutch merchant fluit)
artist: Wenceslaus Hollar (etching, series Navium variae figurae et formae)
what_it_shows: A three-masted merchant ship under sail, crew on deck, other ships on the horizon; the ordinary ocean-going cargo ship of the 1640s.
how_close: The right kind of ship, drawn from life three years after his 1644 crossing; but a Dutch fluit, not the French ship he sailed on, and no port is named.
source_note: Rijksmuseum RP-P-OB-11.354 (hdl.handle.net/10934/RM0001.COLLECT.32421), via Commons; 7206x4442.
rights: CC0 (Rijksmuseum public-domain dedication): Commons page carries {{CC-zero}}; the print is 1647, Hollar d. 1677.
credit_line: Wenceslaus Hollar, "Navis Mercatoria Hollandica, vulgo Vliet," Navium variae figurae et formae, 1647. Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam (CC0).
fit: A 1647 merchant ship, three years after 1644: era exact, the ship a Dutch type rather than his French one.

title: Dieppe
artist: Christophe Tassin (etching, Les plans et profils)
what_it_shows: Bird's-eye plan of walled Dieppe with its harbour channel and ships in the roadstead.
how_close: Dieppe was one of the two usual ports for Quebec in the 1640s (with La Rochelle); which port Eustache sailed from is not established here.
source_note: Bibliothèque municipale de Reims, via Commons; 3355x2403 grayscale.
rights: Public domain: {{PD-old}} on the Commons page.
credit_line: Christophe Tassin, "Dieppe," Les plans et profils des principales villes de France (Paris, 1634/38). Bibliothèque municipale de Reims, via Wikimedia Commons.
fit: Dieppe c.1634-38, a likely but unconfirmed port of departure, 6-10 years before 1644.

title: Abitation de Quebecq
artist: Samuel de Champlain (engraving in Les Voyages du sieur de Champlain, Paris 1613)
what_it_shows: Champlain's fortified wooden habitation at the foot of the cliff: storehouse, dovecote, lodgings, gallery, moat and cannon platforms on the St. Lawrence shore.
how_close: Quebec's founding post as Champlain drew it 31 years before Eustache arrived; it was rebuilt in stone in 1624, so in 1644 the lower town looked different.
source_note: BAnQ Flickr upload (Public Domain Mark), FlickreviewR-passed, via Commons; 1648x2161 page scan, cropped above the legend.
rights: Public domain: Commons page carries {{PD-author-FlickrPDM}} (BAnQ's Public Domain Mark); published 1613.
credit_line: Samuel de Champlain, "Abitation de Quebecq," Les Voyages du sieur de Champlain (Paris, 1613). Bibliothèque et Archives nationales du Québec.
fit: Quebec 1608/1613, 31 years before he arrived: place exact, era early.

title: Quebec veu de l'Est (Vues de la ville de Québec)
artist: Charles Bécart de Fonville (manuscript drawing, Service hydrographique de la Marine)
what_it_shows: Quebec from the east: upper town on the cliff with church spires, lower town at the water, ships and canoes in the basin (cropped from the decorative frame).
how_close: The earliest good view of the whole town, 55 years after 1644 and long after Eustache had moved across the river.
source_note: BnF, Cartes et plans, GE SH 18 PF 127 DIV 7 P 20 (ark:/12148/btv1b5968907s), via Commons; 10896x6992.
rights: Public domain: {{PD-France}} and {{PD-US-expired}} on the Commons page.
credit_line: Charles Bécart de Fonville, "Quebec veu de l'Est," 1699. Bibliothèque nationale de France, Cartes et plans.
fit: Quebec 1699, 55 years after 1644: place exact, era late.

title: La France apportant la foi aux Hurons de la Nouvelle-France
artist: Anonymous (oil on canvas; attribution debated; not checked here)
what_it_shows: A crowned France in a fleur-de-lis mantle shows a kneeling Huron man a painting of the Trinity; mission chapels on the shore, a French ship in the bay, the heavens above.
how_close: The Jesuits' own image of their Huron mission, painted for the Jesuit college at Quebec 17 years after Sainte-Marie burned in 1649. An allegory, not a view of Huronia.
source_note: Photograph after restoration by the Centre de conservation du Québec (ccq.gouv.qc.ca); painting owned by the Ursulines de Québec. 4752x4741.
rights: Public domain: Commons page carries {{PD-scan|PD-old-100}} and {{PD-old-70-1923}}.
credit_line: Anonymous, La France apportant la foi aux Hurons de la Nouvelle-France, c. 1666. Ursulines de Québec; photo Centre de conservation du Québec.
fit: The Jesuit Huron mission as the Jesuits pictured it, c.1666, 17-20 years after 1646-49: era close, place symbolic, not Sainte-Marie.

title: A View of the City of Quebec, the Capital of Canada, taken partly from Pointe des Pères
artist: Hervey Smyth (drawn), Peter Paul Benazech (engraved)
what_it_shows: Quebec across the river from Pointe-des-Pères on the Lévy shore, British warships in the foreground, one firing.
how_close: Drawn from the Lauzon shore itself (Pointe-des-Pères, where Wolfe's batteries stood) during or right after the 1759 siege; the family's side of the river is behind the artist.
source_note: John Carter Brown Library 6367-001, via BnF Gallica (ark:/12148/btv1b101063919) and Commons; 7239x5674, cropped above the caption.
rights: Public domain: {{PD-France}}, {{PD-old-auto-expired|1811}}, {{PD-US-expired}} on the Commons page.
credit_line: Hervey Smyth, del.; P. Benazech, sculp., "A View of the City of Quebec, the Capital of Canada" (London: Jefferys, 1760). John Carter Brown Library, via BnF Gallica.
fit: Quebec from Pointe-des-Pères, 1759-60: place exact (the Lévy shore looking across), era exact.

title: A General View of Quebec, from Point Levy
artist: Richard Short (drawn), Pierre-Charles Canot (engraved)
what_it_shows: Quebec across the basin from the Point Levy shore, with figures and boats on the near (Lévy) bank and ships at anchor.
how_close: The view from the family's shore, drawn by a British naval purser in 1759-60. Only a 1376 px copy was found; not enlarged.
source_note: Commons copy sourced from a Université Laval thesis (theses.ulaval.ca); 1376x898. Better scans exist (LAC C-000355 and others) but were not downloadable here.
rights: Public domain: {{PD-old-70-1923}} on the Commons page; published 1761.
credit_line: Richard Short, del.; P. Canot, sculp., "A General View of Quebec, from Point Levy" (London, 1761).
fit: Quebec from Point Levy, 1761: place exact, era exact; low resolution.

title: Bringing in Burned Refugees from Duluth District
artist: American Red Cross photographer (caption card: "ARC, Mr. Curtis"; plate marked "McKenzie 4413")
what_it_shows: Soldiers, Red Cross nurses and townspeople crowd round a burned fire refugee on a stretcher beside a motor car, after the 12 October 1918 fires.
how_close: The same fire, days later, in the Duluth relief effort that took in Cloquet's evacuees; not Cloquet itself, and the person shown is not identified.
source_note: LOC Prints & Photographs, American National Red Cross collection, LC-A6195-3224; TIFF master 9985x7290 glass negative scan, cropped to the image.
rights: LOC rights advisory: "No known restrictions on publication." (American National Red Cross photograph collection.)
credit_line: American National Red Cross photograph collection, Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division, LC-A6195-3224.
fit: The October 1918 fire's relief, Duluth district: era exact, place about 20 miles from Cloquet.

title: Cloquet city schools and teachers
artist: Smith's Studio (real-photo postcard)
what_it_shows: A montage postcard: Cloquet's high school, Garfield, Washington and other schools, and the teaching staff.
how_close: Cloquet itself eight years before the fire; most of these buildings burned in 1918.
source_note: LOC Prints & Photographs, PCRD 4 - Minnesota - Cloquet, no. 1; copyright deposit J 140191; TIFF master 3352x2153.
rights: LOC rights advisory: "Rights status not evaluated." Published 1910 with notice, so public domain in the US (pre-1930 publication).
credit_line: Smith's Studio, "Cloquet city schools and teachers," postcard, 1910. Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division.
fit: Cloquet 1910: place exact, eight years before the fire and 16 years after the family's 1894 start there.

title: Main St., Int. Falls, Minn.
artist: I.P. & I. Co. (real-photo postcard)
what_it_shows: Main Street, International Falls: shops, a pool parlour and drugstore, a buggy, summer crowds, and the mill smokestack at the end of the street.
how_close: The town itself in the middle of the family's years there (c.1910-1928); the paper mill shows only as the stack at the end of the street.
source_note: LOC Prints & Photographs, PCRD 4 - Minnesota - International Falls, no. 3; copyright J 184124; TIFF master 3397x2197.
rights: LOC rights advisory: "Rights status not evaluated." Published 1913 with notice, so public domain in the US (pre-1930 publication).
credit_line: "Main St., Int. Falls, Minn.," postcard, ©1913 I.P. & I. Co. Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division.
fit: International Falls 1913: place exact, era exact (inside c.1910-1928).

title: A mountain of pulp wood: 40,000 cords in pile, Int. Falls, Minn.
artist: I.P. & I. Co. (real-photo postcard)
what_it_shows: A conveyor feeding a pulpwood pile of 40,000 cords at the International Falls paper mill.
